===MONITOR-SECTION:config===
# config.default -- seed for the per-device worker config.
#
# 03-build-state.sh copies this to <state>/transcode/config ONLY IF that file is
# absent, so a box's own edits are never clobbered by a re-run of 03. The file
# lives on the per-device state export: it survives reboots, it is per-device by
# construction, and it is read at the start of EVERY pass, so a change takes
# effect without a reboot and without a redeploy.
#
# Format: KEY=value, one per line, # comments. There is exactly ONE reader: the
# worker's load_config(). It validates the key name, skips anything that is not
# [A-Za-z0-9_], and refuses a short deny-list of shell-critical names (IFS, PATH,
# LD_PRELOAD and friends), so a corrupted line cannot inject a command or break
# everything downstream of it.
#
# The unit deliberately carries NO EnvironmentFile= pointing at this file. It
# used to, and that made this file inert: systemd set the keys in the
# environment before bash started, load_config is environment-WINS, and so every
# value here was shadowed by the unit's identical copy -- an edit took effect
# only after a service restart, silently. Do not add it back. Two readers of one
# fact is the defect, not the redundancy.
#
# Environment-WINS is still the rule, and it is what makes `TOTAL=2
# ./worker.sh --dry-run` a safe way to try a setting without editing this file.
# The worker re-reads this file at the top of every pass, so a change here lands
# on the next pass; a value supplied on the command line is never unset by that
# reload, so the two mechanisms do not fight.
#
# Effective values, with the config file accounted for, come from
# `transcode-ctl show-config`. Do not read defaults out of this file: it is a
# SEED, and every key here is also defaulted in worker.sh.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sharding. The fleet splits the library by md5 of each file's path RELATIVE to
# the recordings root, modulo TOTAL, and each box takes the residue equal to its
# own index (cubox-1 -> 0, cubox-2 -> 1).
#
#   TOTAL=1  every box considers every file (correct for one box, and the
#            starting point: it duplicates work if a second box is also at 1)
#   TOTAL=2  the library is split; each box takes half
#
# MIGRATION ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, AND THE RULE IS: NEVER NARROW A CLAIM BEFORE
# SOMETHING ELSE COVERS WHAT YOU DROP.
#
#   ENROLLING A NEW BOX -- bring cubox-2 UP at TOTAL=2 FIRST, then raise cubox-1
#   to 2. While cubox-1 is still at 1 it claims every file, so the overlap is
#   duplication (harmless); once it is at 2 it holds the evens and cubox-2 holds
#   the odds. There is no instant at which a file is claimed by nobody.
#
#   The reverse -- cubox-1 to 2 first -- NARROWS cubox-1 to the evens while
#   cubox-2 is not yet doing passes, and nothing claims the odds until it starts.
#   That window is a real GAP, and neither box can see it: each only ever asks
#   "is this file mine?", and for those files the honest answer on both is "no".
#
# THIS PARAGRAPH SAID THE OPPOSITE UNTIL 2026-09-25, and its worked example was
# arithmetically wrong. It read "raise TOTAL on cubox-1 FIRST", justified by
# "if cubox-2 is set to 2 while cubox-1 is still at 1, every file with md5 % 2 == 1
# is owned by nobody". That is not true: at TOTAL=1 the modulus is 1, residue 0 is
# the only class, and cubox-1 claims EVERY file -- odds included. Nothing is
# unowned in that state; cubox-2 merely duplicates. The old rule is gap-free for
# two boxes that are both already running a worker, which is presumably where it
# came from -- and it is wrong in the one situation anyone actually reads it, a
# box being enrolled.
#
# `scripts/11-transcode-verify.sh` is what settles this rather than the reasoning
# above: it computes ownership from each box's LIVE (TOTAL, MY_INDEX), unions the
# per-box claim files against the source listing, and reports GAP as a hard error.
# Run it after changing this number. Reason, then measure.
#
# The shard is a work-distribution HINT, not ownership. The only correctness
# criterion is the done-test, so a mis-set TOTAL moves work around rather than
# corrupting anything. TOTAL unset or garbage is coerced to 1 with a loud
# CONFIG-BAD line, because modulus 0 makes every file read "not mine" -- a total
# stall that looks exactly like a quiet box.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# SEED VALUE, and worth distinguishing from what a running box uses. This file is
# the seed for a box with no stored config (a first enrolment, or --force). A box
# that has one reads /mnt/state/transcode/config instead, so changing this line
# does NOT change a box that is already enrolled -- that config must be edited
# too, and it is the authority for its keys.
#
# 2 rather than 1 since 2026-09-25, because the fleet is now two boxes. At 1 a
# second box duplicates the first one's entire workload while looking healthy.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL=2

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How many times a file may FAIL before it is skipped for good. Environment
# failures (NAS gone, output unwritable, ffmpeg missing) deliberately do NOT
# count against this: an outage must not walk the library into a permanent skip
# list. See `transcode-ctl clear-skip` to undo a skip after fixing the cause.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MAX_ATTEMPTS=3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Progressive fast path. 1 = when a source is already h264 with
# field_order=progressive, copy the video and transcode only the audio
# (measured 1.36x realtime on 24 CPU-s, against 0.30x for a full transcode).
#
# This fires ZERO times on the current library: all 13 recordings probe
# field_order=tt. It is kept because it costs one ffprobe and guards future
# content -- do not expect it to shorten this backlog.
#
# The gate is exact string equality against one ffprobe line, so every other
# outcome (empty, tt/bb/tb/bt, an error, a renamed field) takes the yadif path.
# No branch can invent "progressive".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FASTPATH=1

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# An output smaller than this is NOT considered done, and the worker will
# re-transcode over it. The size floor is not decoration: the transcoded tree
# already holds 12 zero-byte mp4s from a prior silent failure, and an
# existence-only test would treat them as finished forever. With the floor they
# are simply redone and the atomic rename replaces them -- no manual cleanup.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MIN_BYTES=1048576

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Ignore source files modified in the last N minutes. A file still being written
# by the PVR recorder would otherwise be transcoded mid-write, and the duration
# check would pass against a growing source. Deferrals are counted as
# `deferred`, never as `done`.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECENT_MIN=15

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Video bitrate. LEAVE THIS UNSET.
#
# Unset means "derive it": the worker reads the source container bitrate and
# uses 1.2x, clamped to [2500k, 12000k]. Measured sources are 3.45-5.10 Mb/s, so
# derived rates land at 4140k-6120k. The container rate includes audio and
# teletext, and AAC replaces the mp2 track, so 1.2x slightly over-provisions the
# video -- which is the conservative direction.
#
# Setting it forces ONE rate on every file and overrides the derivation. The
# VPU encoder has no CRF, only a target bitrate, so this is the only lever on
# output size. Operator decision was to match the source.
#
# BR=8000k
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# AAC audio bitrate for the output.
AUDIO_BR=192k

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Seconds of source used by --probe-run, the acceptance test. Not used by a real
# pass. 60 s at the measured 0.327x takes about three minutes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAP_SEG=60

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Loop pacing. IDLE_JOBS is the pause after a pass that did work; IDLE_EMPTY
# after a pass that found nothing, so an exhausted library does not spin.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
IDLE_JOBS=10
IDLE_EMPTY=300

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Free-space guard: at pass start the output must have at least this many times
# the largest source file free. Covers the output, the in-flight .part, and the
# once-only +faststart rewrite. The worker reads the df VALUE, not its exit
# status (item 29).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FREE_FACTOR=3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VPU encoder capture-buffer pool. THIS IS THE DEADLOCK'S SWITCH -- measured
# 2026-09-25/26, and it had been documented as settled by inference alone.
#
# The driver default AND this knob's floor are both 4, and at 4 the source-EOF
# drain deadlocks on an infinite poll() (item 52). 16 was adopted as the fix and
# is NOT sufficient: five jobs deadlocked at 16 with the value confirmed in the
# running argv. The measurement that settles it -- cubox-1, same source
# (`Futurama_2026-09-19_10-30.ts`), same day, only this value changed:
#
#     arm 16: DEADLOCK  rc=137   9199 s  last frame 44987  drain-warn 1  corrupt 234
#     arm 64: COMPLETED rc=0     5588 s  last frame 44989  drain-warn 0  corrupt 229
#
# The 16-buffer arm left a 1,019,215,920-byte file with NO moov -- present,
# unplayable, and precisely why "an artifact exists" is not the test:
# verify_artifact() checks six things, not one.
#
# IT IS NOT A MEMORY TRADE, which is the obvious thing to suspect and was
# measured: peak RSS was 136,120 kB at 16 and 135,180 kB at 64, and CmaFree sat
# at 0 kB during BOTH runs -- one 1080p job saturates ~260 MB of the 256 MB CMA
# pool at either size -- returning to ~52 MB after a clean exit. The prediction
# that 64 could not be ALLOCATED from that pool (recorded in scripts/14's header)
# was falsified: it allocated and encoded normally.
#
# n=3 for "64 removes it", and the second and third are the production path rather
# than a diagnostic -- each file compared against its OWN failing run at 16:
#   `09-25_16-55`  deadlock at 16 (stall-killed, frame 44974) -> PUBLISHED at 64,
#                  verify ok, 975.2 MiB, duration 1000/1000, 5403 s wall
#   `09-19_11-00`  deadlock at 16 at frame 44979 on BOTH boxes -> PUBLISHED at 64,
#                  verify ok, 1044.9 MiB, duration 1000/1000, 5418 s wall
#   `09-19_10-30`  cap-killed at 16 on attempt 2 -> PUBLISHED at 64 in 5496 s
# All three had sat at 2/3 strikes, one failure short of permanent retirement, so
# all three runs also rescued them. Still not proof that no source can exhaust the
# pool. That is exactly why the stall watchdog below STAYS: it bounds a recurrence
# to 300 s instead of the 3 h 05 m cap, and it is what makes this value safe to
# RAISE rather than safe to TRUST.
#
# AND 16 IS NOT UNIFORMLY FATAL, which is worth knowing before reading the table
# above as "16 is broken". Measured 2026-09-25T23:47Z, cubox-2 COMPLETED and
# PUBLISHED `Futurama_2026-09-25_17-25.ts` (2100 s, the longest source here) at
# `-num_capture_buffers 16`, confirmed in its argv: verify ok, 1162.3 MiB,
# duration 1000/1000, 6471 s wall. So the tally at 16 is five full-length
# deadlocks and one full-length success. The pool size does not by itself decide
# it; nothing measured yet predicts which sources fail.
#
# AND ONE MORE, INFERRED RATHER THAN READ. `09-22_17-30` stalled 66 s in (frame
# 1649 of ~45013 -- nowhere near EOF) and burned the full cap on 2026-09-25. Its
# argv is gone, but the state config's mtime (2026-09-25T23:38:24Z) postdates that
# run, and cubox-2's identical window is MEASURED at 16 -- so attempt 1 was at 16,
# and at 64 it published on 2026-09-26 (956.0 MiB, duration 999/1000, 5388 s). That
# makes it very probably a fifth 16-dies/64-lives case, and the only non-EOF one.
# It is NOT counted in the n=3 above: a pool size inferred from an mtime is not one
# read from an argv. item 70 of docs/08-forensic-lessons.md states the chain.
#
# That run is also the corruption question's answer, and it closes it. Its
# retained log reads 308 corrupt frames over 52457 = 5.9 per 1000 -- at the TOP
# of the deadlocking files' 4.7-5.7 range. A successful run is not less corrupt
# than a failing one, so corruption is not the discriminator. (The log itself was
# deleted by the publish; it survives only because a snapshotter was copying it
# every 20 s. A success destroys its own evidence -- see item 65's converse.)
#
# Delivery is a config edit, and it takes effect on the next pass -- no reboot, no
# redeploy, no rebuild. That is the intended shape for a per-device knob.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CAPTURE_BUFFERS=64

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stall watchdog: how a stalled encode is ended, and this pair exists because
# nothing else ends one.
#
# The VPU encoder deadlocks on the source-EOF drain (item 52): `enc0:0:h264_v4l`
# parks in an infinite poll(), every other ffmpeg thread parks behind it, and the
# frame counter never moves again. `-num_capture_buffers 16` does not prevent it
# -- measured on both boxes 2026-09-25, with 16 confirmed present in the argv.
# Raising the pool to 64 DID remove it on the one file where that was tested (see
# the CAPTURE_BUFFERS stanza above), and this watchdog stays anyway: an untested
# recurrence on some other source is the case it exists for.
# Before this watchdog existed the only thing that ended such a job was the
# wall-clock cap, 6x the source duration plus 300 s: 3 h 05 m for a 30-minute
# episode, ending in no artifact and one strike against the file.
#
# THE PRODUCT IS THE KNOB. STALL_SAMPLES x STALL_POLL is the number of seconds the
# frame counter must be frozen before the encode is killed, and it must stay
# ABOVE the ~180 s `-movflags +faststart` tail -- because a HEALTHY job freezes
# its output for that long at the end while ffmpeg rewrites the moov atom. What
# separates the two is the stderr log: a healthy finalize is SILENT, a deadlock
# keeps writing an identical record every 500 ms. See stall_watch() in worker.sh,
# which requires BOTH halves and is the only reason this is safe to enable.
#
# 15 x 20 = 300 s: 1.7x the measured faststart window, and 37x shorter than the
# cap it replaces. Raising STALL_SAMPLES lowers the false-positive risk; lowering
# it toward the faststart figure is how you kill healthy encodes.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
STALL_POLL=15
STALL_SAMPLES=20

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths. These are defaults the worker also carries; listed here so an operator
# can see and override them without reading the script.
#
# SRC_ROOT is the recordings tree (automounted read-only).
# TRANSCODED_PATH is the Storage-NAS filesystem path as seen FROM THE NAS. The
# NFS export path for Storage-NAS takes the FULL form -- the opposite of
# Backup-NAS, whose exports are matched by the short name `showmount -e` prints
# (item 20).
#
# Note the output tree is the EXISTING transcoded/ directory, shared with the
# x86 transcode pool. Atomic rename makes that collision harmless -- wasted
# work, never corruption.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SRC_ROOT=/mnt/recordings
STORAGE_IP=198.51.100.10
TRANSCODED_PATH=/share/CACHEDEV1_DATA/Programs/pvr/media/transcoded

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Overriding where output lands. Normally UNSET, and the worker DERIVES it:
# /mnt/transcoded if that directory exists (Phase B, baked into the image), else
# /build/out (Phase A, under a tmpfs the boot hook already mounts).
#
# Setting OUT_ROOT bypasses the derivation. It is here for a trial run against a
# scratch tree; leaving it set in production would point the worker at a path
# whose mount nothing else maintains. The derivation is deliberately additive so
# a Phase A worker keeps working across the Phase B rebuild with no edit.
#
# OUT_ROOT=/build/out
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
